guide.title: Guide
guide.subtitle: A tour of what Vibisual can do — and an inventory of features built so far.

start.intro: Vibisual visualizes what your AI agents are doing, in real time, as a bubble map.
start.openFolderD: File → Open Folder to start tracking a project. Each project opens in its own tab.
start.watchD: When Claude Code runs, the files and folders it touches appear as bubbles and pulse as they change.
start.optionsD: File → Options to choose the default model, tools, permission mode and Claude Code binary for new agents.

bubbleMap.intro: The canvas draws your project as bubbles linked by hierarchy and activity.
bubbleMap.typesD: Files, folders, agents, Bash, edits, iframes and more — each color-coded by category.
bubbleMap.sizeD: Bigger bubbles were touched more often. A pulsing bubble is active right now.
bubbleMap.contextD: An agent bubble fills like water to show how much of its context window is in use.
bubbleMap.ghostD: Deleted or renamed nodes linger as faded ghosts so the trail isn't lost.

agents.intro: Beyond passive tracking, you can create and orchestrate your own agents from the canvas.
agents.customD: Right-click the canvas to spawn your own agent bubble and give it a command.
agents.autoD: Describe what you want in plain language; a builder agent designs and wires up a whole team for you.
agents.configD: Click a bubble to set its model, tools, permission mode, effort, isolation and color.
agents.pipelineD: Run independent sessions and chain agents together with pipeline, teams or hybrid strategies.

taskEdges.intro: Connect two custom agents with a Task Edge to delegate work between them.
taskEdges.drawD: Drag from one custom-agent bubble to another to create a delegation edge between them.
taskEdges.kindsD: Command, artifact, request or critique — the kind says what flows across the edge.
taskEdges.critiqueD: A critique edge can force the target agent to rework its output until a reviewer accepts it.

ide.intro: Double-click an agent to open the IDE overlay — its live output, sessions and reports.
ide.streamD: Follow the agent's messages, tool calls and results as they happen.
ide.cardsD: Finished work and things you need to do yourself are split into color-coded cards.
ide.reviewD: When an agent finishes a fix, a purple card shows what changed and what to check.
ide.dockD: Drag the overlay's title bar to float it, or snap it to the right as a side panel.

navigation.panD: Drag the canvas to pan and scroll to zoom; the minimap shows where you are.
navigation.tabsD: Each open folder is a tab; drag a tab out of the bar to pop it into its own window.
navigation.inspectorD: Hold Alt to highlight elements and click to copy; Shift-drag to select a region.
navigation.copyD: Select custom agents and edges, then {{copy}} / {{paste}} to clone them into another project.

history.intro: Vibisual remembers your projects between runs.
history.saveD: The whole graph is checkpointed to disk and restored the next time you open Vibisual.
history.replayD: Scrub a timeline to replay how the map grew over a session.

shortcuts.intro: Keyboard shortcuts speed up navigation and editing. They pause while you type in an input or terminal.
shortcuts.inspectorD: Hold Alt to inspect and click to copy an element; Shift-drag for region select.
shortcuts.closeD: Esc closes menus, popups and the IDE overlay.
shortcuts.remapNote: Click the pencil on a shortcut to change it — conflicts are checked as you press. {{options}} › {{keyboard}} has the full list with search, import and export.

autoGoal.intro: Procedure detection watches what you and your agents actually repeat, and writes the repeated work down as a reusable procedure. It ships turned off — you switch it on per project, per agent or per session.
autoGoal.turnOnD: Open {{procedures}} in the activity bar. Three switches stack there — whole project, this agent, this session — and the lower one overrides the one above it. Each click cycles On → Off → Inherit.
autoGoal.watchesD: Runs of shell commands an agent actually executed, and step groups you pinned to the stage yourself. Nothing is sent anywhere — the analysis is a plain count that happens on this machine.
autoGoal.thresholdD: A run has to come back the same way several times before it becomes a procedure. Until then it sits in the candidate list with a progress bar, so you can see what is about to be written.
autoGoal.filesD: Each one is a plain SKILL.md under .vibisual/skills in your project, with the agentskills.io frontmatter. Open it, edit it, commit it — a file you edited by hand is never overwritten.
autoGoal.promptD: Only the name, one line of description and the file path. The body stays on disk and the agent opens it when the work matches, so twenty procedures still cost almost nothing.
autoGoal.dismissD: Dismissing a candidate stops the suggestion, it does not erase the observation. The same run can keep happening — procedure detection simply stops offering to write it down.
autoGoal.keepsD: Switching it off stops the analysis, not the storage. Procedures already written stay in your project and are yours to keep, and nothing is ever deleted automatically.

advanced.terminalScrollbackDesc: How many output lines a CMD terminal keeps. Scrolling and {{shortcut}} search share this range. Applies to terminals opened from now on.
advanced.bgProbeIntro: A background command that goes quiet is not necessarily finished — one that waits for something is quiet by design, so Vibisual never closes an item on elapsed time alone. Instead, when an item has been quiet for a long while with no end marker, a small judging agent is asked once whether the command has a condition under which it ends by itself and whether that condition is already met.
advanced.bgProbeEnabledDesc: Off means no model is ever called for this — quiet items simply stay on the list until you remove them.
advanced.bgProbeQuietDesc: Silence only decides when to ask — it never decides the answer. 0 turns the asking off.
advanced.bgProbeAutoClose: Clear the item when the answer is "finished"
advanced.bgProbeAutoCloseDesc: Off means the answer is only written onto the card and you decide. "Still running" and "could not tell" never clear anything either way.
advanced.bgProbeKill: Also stop the processes it had started
advanced.bgProbeKillDesc: Clearing the list alone leaves the command running. Only processes under that session whose command line matches this task are touched.
advanced.bgProbeModelDesc: It is asked once, with no tools and no access to your project — only the command text and a short tail of its output.
advanced.bgProbeLoadError: Could not read the current setting.
advanced.bgProbeSaveError: Could not save. Nothing was changed.
advanced.sessionProbeIntro: A session can sit on "running" long after its work ended, because the signals that end a session are all self-reported — if one is missed, nothing takes it down. Elapsed time cannot settle it either: a session waiting on a long build looks exactly like one that quietly died. So every 10 minutes a small judging agent is asked once, about a single session, what it is waiting for and whether that is still coming.
advanced.sessionProbeEnabled: Check whether running sessions are really running
advanced.sessionProbeEnabledDesc: Off means no model is ever called for this — sessions stay on "running" until something else takes them down.
advanced.sessionProbeQuietDesc: Silence only decides when to ask — it never decides the answer. A session that answers "still working" is left alone for longer and longer before being asked again. 0 turns the asking off.
advanced.sessionProbeAutoClose: End the session when the answer is "finished"
advanced.sessionProbeAutoCloseDesc: Off means the answer is only shown in the status bar and you decide. "Still working", "stuck" and "could not tell" never end anything either way — and nothing here kills a process; the session is simply marked as no longer running.
advanced.sessionProbeModelDesc: It is asked once, with no tools and no access to your project — only a short tail of what that session last said and did. At most one session is asked at a time, and no more than 12 times an hour.
advanced.sessionProbeLoadError: Could not read the current setting.
advanced.sessionProbeSaveError: Could not save. Nothing was changed.
advanced.processGuardIntro: Everything an agent runs here, and everything that starts in turn however deep it goes, stays under Vibisual’s watch. If one process runs away with memory, only that process is stopped, and when a session ends whatever it left behind ends with it. A single command can no longer use up the computer’s memory and take the app down with it.
advanced.processGuardEnabledDesc: Off means nothing is grouped, capped or cleaned up — the way it was before this option existed.
advanced.processGuardCap: Memory one process may use (% of RAM)
advanced.processGuardCapDesc: A process that goes over this is stopped. The limit never goes below {{floor}}, so large builds still fit. 0 means no limit. On Windows the system itself refuses the extra memory; elsewhere Vibisual checks every {{seconds}} seconds.
advanced.processGuardCapNone: On this computer: no limit per process
advanced.processGuardPressure: When memory runs out, stop the largest one
advanced.processGuardPressureDesc: When free memory falls below {{ratio}} (at least {{min}}), the largest process your agents started is stopped — one at a time, then memory is measured again. Other programs on your computer are never touched.
advanced.processGuardReap: Clean up what a session leaves behind
advanced.processGuardReapDesc: When a session ends, or Claude Code reports that it stopped a task, processes still left over from it are stopped too. Off leaves them running.
advanced.engineBridgeIntro: Sessions that Vibisual starts carry a small Claude Code mod. From inside Claude Code it reports when a turn starts and ends (including turns you interrupt), that the process is still alive, and how full the context and usage limits are. Running and finished states then come from Claude Code itself instead of being guessed. Sessions you start outside Vibisual are never touched.
advanced.engineBridgeEnabled: Connect the sessions Vibisual starts (headless and CMD)
advanced.engineBridgeEnabledDesc: Applies to sessions started after saving. Off means sessions run exactly as before, with their state taken from hooks and screen detection only.
advanced.engineBridgeStatusReady: Claude Code {{version}} can load the bridge. Sessions connected right now: {{sessions}}
advanced.engineBridgeStatusUnsupported: Claude Code {{version}} cannot load mods; version {{min}} or later is needed. Sessions run as before.
advanced.engineBridgeStatusChecking: Checking the Claude Code version. The bridge joins from the next session once it is confirmed.
advanced.engineBridgeStatusMissing: The bridge files are missing from this installation, so sessions run as before.
advanced.engineBridgeStatusError: Could not read the bridge status.
advanced.externalBudgetIntro: When an agent touches a folder outside the project, that place gets its own bubble. Left alone, those bubbles either bury the map or collapse into one that says nothing. This number sets how many of them stand at the top level at once — the busiest and most recent places fill it first, and places that go quiet fold back under their parent.
advanced.externalBudgetLabel: External folders shown at the top level
advanced.externalBudgetDesc: Pinned folders do not count against this number — a folder you pinned always stays at the top level. Nothing is deleted by this setting: places that do not fit are folded under a parent bubble that tells you how many are inside.
advanced.externalBudgetLoadError: Could not read the current setting.
advanced.externalBudgetSaveError: Could not save. Nothing was changed.
advanced.webFoldIntro: When an agent reads the web, every domain it reads becomes a bubble, so one agent researching can cover the canvas. These settings group them — nothing is deleted, and clicking a group lists its domains one by one.
advanced.webGroupSameSite: Group domains of the same site
advanced.webGroupSameSiteDesc: Subdomains of one site, like docs.github.com and github.com, share a single bubble named after the site.
advanced.webGroupByKindDesc: When there are more than the number below, sites of the same kind — docs, code, packages, Q&A and so on — share one bubble. Sites whose kind is unclear go into "{{other}}".
advanced.webGroupMaxLabel: Web bubbles shown separately per agent
advanced.webGroupMaxDesc: Up to this many stand on their own, the most recently read first; the rest are grouped. 1 folds everything an agent read into one bubble, and 0 means no limit. Pinned domains always keep their own bubble and do not count.
advanced.webOpenTargetDesc: Double-clicking a web bubble opens the last address it read (for the search bubble, the last search).
advanced.webOpenTargetExternalDesc: The default. Opens in the browser you normally use.
advanced.webOpenTargetIframeDesc: Opens a web tab in the tab bar so you can read it inside the app. Internet pages run in a separate sandboxed view with no permissions, and sign-ins are cleared when the app closes.

permissions.verificationGateIntro: This policy applies to both Codex and Claude Code only when enabled. Then agents are told to run tests, lint, type checks, verification builds, E2E, browser checks, screenshot comparisons and verification agents only when requested in the current task, and unrequested calls are blocked before execution.
permissions.verificationGateEnabled: Require a request before running verification
permissions.verificationGateEnabledDesc: Off by default. When off, Vibisual adds no verification restriction to prompts and does not block calls under this policy. When on, script names containing check, verify or test may also be blocked. Save with {{apply}}: blocking changes from the next tool call, and prompt guidance from the next turn.

tokenSaver.title: Token saving
tokenSaver.intro: Almost all of what you pay for is re-reading: measured over five hours, 96.5% of input tokens were the conversation being sent again on the next turn. So the two things worth controlling are how much lands in context per turn, and how many turns it gets re-read across. Every setting here is one of those two, and 0 always means that one is off.
tokenSaver.presetDesc: Presets only fill in the fields below — nothing is applied until you save. Off is byte-for-byte the behaviour you had before this screen existed.
tokenSaver.bashMaxOutputChars: Max characters of shell output kept in context
tokenSaver.bashMaxOutputCharsDesc: The single biggest source of context growth. Output that lands once is re-read on every later turn of that session, so cutting it here cuts it for the whole session. 0 leaves the CLI default (30,000).
tokenSaver.mcpMaxOutputTokens: Max tokens of MCP tool output
tokenSaver.mcpMaxOutputTokensDesc: Same idea for MCP tools. Nothing changes for agents with no MCP server attached. 0 leaves the CLI default.
tokenSaver.maxOutputTokens: Max tokens the model writes per turn
tokenSaver.maxOutputTokensDesc: Written tokens cost about five times what read tokens do, and everything written also stays in context. Set too low, answers get cut mid-sentence and you pay again to redo them. 0 leaves the model default.
tokenSaver.maxThinkingTokensDesc: Caps the length of extended thinking. Separate from turning thinking on or off, and from the effort level. 0 leaves the model default.
tokenSaver.autoCompactPct: Compact when the window is this full (%)
tokenSaver.autoCompactPctDesc: Folds the conversation earlier than the default. Only lower values take effect. Compacting is itself a large request, so folding too often costs more than it saves. 0 leaves the CLI default.
tokenSaver.maxConcurrentAgents: Sessions allowed to run at the same time
tokenSaver.maxConcurrentAgentsDesc: Sixteen sessions running at once cost sixteen times as much at once. Commands over the limit are never dropped — they wait in their queue and go out as soon as a slot frees. Terminals you type in yourself are not counted. 0 means no limit.
tokenSaver.spawnStaggerMsDesc: Sessions started at the same instant cannot reuse each other's cached prefix, so each writes its own from scratch. A short gap lets the later ones read the cache instead at a tenth of the price. Only applies to brand-new sessions. 0 means no gap.
tokenSaver.sessionTurnBudget: Compact a session after this many turns
tokenSaver.sessionTurnBudgetDesc: A long session re-reads its whole history every turn, so the cost of leaving one running grows with the square of its length. This folds it once the turn count is reached. It never starts a new session — your conversation is kept. 0 means no limit.
tokenSaver.disableNonEssential: Skip background model calls for titles and summaries
tokenSaver.disableNonEssentialDesc: These are small extra calls the CLI makes for conveniences. Session tab names here are derived from your first prompt without calling a model, so turning this on costs you almost nothing visible.
tokenSaver.loadError: Could not read the current setting.
tokenSaver.saveError: Could not save. Nothing was changed.
tokenSaver.autoCompactWindow: Fold the conversation once it reaches
tokenSaver.autoCompactWindowDesc: The largest single lever here. Measured over three days, sessions sat at a median of 186k tokens and everything above 200k accounted for 62% of all input — every turn re-reads that. Lowering the window from 400k to 200k cut input by 27%, and 100k by 59%, for the same work. It only ever tightens: an agent or a default that is already lower wins. Folding is itself a large request, so the lowest setting is not automatically the cheapest. This window only decides where we fold between commands — mid-task, the CLI only folds when the model window fills up.

confirm.title: Turn auto-compact on? ({{value}})
confirm.titleSelf: Let the agent compact on its own?
confirm.costBody: Compaction is not free cleanup — it feeds the whole conversation back to the model to write a summary, as a separate model call. Every fold spends input and output tokens, and your plan usage.
confirm.costSample: Measured example (avg of {{runs}} runs): about {{tokens}} tokens re-read per fold, pausing about {{seconds}} seconds. Your numbers vary with conversation length and model.
confirm.selfBody: The agent asks to compact when it judges the context is heavy, and it runs after that turn ends. Each request is one summarization call, so it costs the same tokens.
confirm.offHeading: What you lose by leaving it off
confirm.offBody: Without folding, the whole accumulated conversation is resent every turn, so cost and latency both climb. When the model window fills, the CLI folds once mid-task — or the session breaks past the window.

lint.network: Network calls (fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket) are blocked. Put the data in the item props instead.
lint.external-url: External URLs are blocked. Copy the file into the composition folder and use a relative path.
lint.media-element: <audio>/<video> cannot follow the timeline. Put sound on an audio track and video as a clip.
lint.sound-api: Sound made in code is silenced. Put sound on an audio track instead.
lint.worker: Web workers are blocked in compositions.
lint.storage: Storage and cookies are not available in compositions.
lint.module-script: Module scripts may not load. Use classic script tags.
lint.css-transition: CSS transitions cannot be scrubbed. Use @keyframes or element.animate().
lint.input-wait: Some code waits for a click or key press — nobody presses keys in a video.
lint.no-duration: No declared length (vibi:duration). Give the clip a duration or declare one in the file.
lint.frame-callbacks: Uses frame callbacks, so it can only play forward — going back replays it from the start.
lint.virtual-clock: Clock and random values are made repeatable for each video.
lint.no-motion: No animation found — this clip may never change over time.
lint.no-props-decl: No values are declared, so the studio can't show handles for this composition.
lint.engine-unsupported: Uses web features the video renderer does not support yet — they are ignored in the video.
lint.perf-background-position: Animating background-position repaints the whole layer every frame. Move the layer with transform instead.
lint.perf-animated-filter: Changing a filter (blur and the like) every frame redraws that whole area each frame. Keep the filter fixed and animate opacity or transform.
lint.perf-blur-shadow: A large blurred box-shadow is slow to redraw. Draw the glow once on its own layer and move or fade that layer.
lint.perf-put-image-data: putImageData over a full-size canvas every frame is slow. Draw small tiles once and move them with transform.
lint.frame-callbacks-seekable: Uses frame callbacks but answers seeks itself, so it can still jump to any time. Anything the callbacks draw must also follow the current time.

loop.clearing: Clearing the context before the next round…

reading.title: Reading settings
reading.resetField: Reset this setting to its default
reading.measureNote: Dyson & Haselgrove measured three different optima: 95 characters per line read fastest, 35 gave the best comprehension, and 55 is the balance point.
reading.chatAlignOn: Align my messages right, AI left
reading.chatAlignNote: Like a messenger app: your prompts hug the right edge and shrink to their text, AI replies stay on the left. Who said what is visible from the position alone, before you read a word. Code, tables and tool boxes keep their full width.
reading.contentWidthNote: Narrows the whole content area — cards, tool boxes, code and tables come inside it as well. Reading width above only narrows the prose column; this narrows everything. 100% is the full window width, and every step down narrows it straight away (10% minimum). Which way it shrinks is decided by Chat alignment above: with it off the content collects in the centre, with it on AI replies stay pinned to the left edge and your prompts to the right edge, so only the opposite side gives way. Narrow windows release it automatically.

skillsPrefix.what: Slash commands Vibisual types in front of your message so the session starts with those skills loaded.
skillsPrefix.more: Comes from the Skills field in Agent Settings. Each skill is sent as a /name line above your prompt.
skillsPrefix.off: Your message is sent on its own and those skills are not invoked.

agentRules.what: Your own standing instructions for this agent bubble.
agentRules.more: Comes from the Agent Rules box in Agent Settings, added under an "# Agent Rules" heading.
agentRules.off: The agent stops receiving those standing instructions.

edges.what: Instructions carried by the arrows you drew from this bubble to other bubbles.
edges.more: Built from this bubble's outgoing task edges — how to hand work over and what to send back.
edges.off: The agent no longer knows what its outgoing arrows expect from it.

feedback.what: Your past thumbs-up / thumbs-down notes on this agent's answers.
feedback.more: Collected from the feedback buttons under earlier answers so the agent repeats what worked.
feedback.off: Past feedback is no longer replayed to the agent.

intentFirst.what: The rule that makes the agent say what it is about to do before it touches any file.
intentFirst.more: A fixed Vibisual instruction. It exists so you can stop the agent early when it heads the wrong way.
intentFirst.off: The agent may start editing files without announcing its plan first. This rule ships once in the system prompt at session start, so turning it off takes effect the next time this session spawns.

cardCommon.what: The one set of rules every card report shares - where to post, when to post, and where the card sits relative to your text.
cardCommon.more: Kept in one place so the same paragraph is not repeated in every card block. It is only included when at least one card is on.
cardCommon.off: The agent no longer knows how to post a card, so the cards below may never appear.

cardReport.what: The recipe for the colored "what I did / what you need to do" card.
cardReport.more: Tells the agent to report its result through Vibisual's API so the two lists can be split by color.
cardReport.off: Results arrive as plain text only — no colored card.

cardQuestion.what: The recipe for question cards with ready-made reply buttons.
cardQuestion.more: When the agent asks you something, it also sends the question and suggested answers as data.
cardQuestion.off: Questions stay buried in the text, with no copy or send buttons.

cardReview.what: The recipe for the purple "please check this" card shown after a fix.
cardReview.more: Tells the agent to list what it changed and what you should click to verify it.
cardReview.off: You get a text summary instead of a review checklist.

cardList.what: The recipe for auto-numbered list cards.
cardList.more: Long enumerations are sent as data so Vibisual numbers and aligns them for you.
cardList.off: Lists are printed inline as ordinary text.

cardIframe.what: The recipe that turns a local server URL into a live preview bubble.
cardIframe.more: When you asked for a server, the agent reports its address and Vibisual opens it on the canvas.
cardIframe.off: Server addresses are only mentioned as text; you open them yourself.

goal.what: This session's goal and its step list, as shown in the goal window.
goal.more: Comes from the goal card so the agent knows where it stands in the plan.
goal.off: The agent stops seeing the goal and its progress list. The goal window itself stays. The half that explains how to update it ships once at session start, so that part drops from the next spawn.

compactRecovery.what: A one-turn note listing what the compaction summary did not appear to carry over.
compactRecovery.more: Built from the snapshot taken just before the compaction, compared against the summary text. It is sent once and never repeated.
compactRecovery.off: Turn it off and the session continues after a compaction with no note about what fell out of the summary.

verificationPolicy.what: Optional guidance for Codex and Claude Code to run verification only when requested in the current task, plus the task's verification permission.
verificationPolicy.more: The policy is off by default. When enabled, Vibisual grants verification permission from your message or the verification button for that task. When disabled, it adds no restrictive guidance and does not block verification calls.
verificationPolicy.off: This source switch only hides the guidance when the policy is enabled. Enable or disable both guidance and execution blocking in {{options}}, under {{permissions}}. The policy is off by default.

hookEnforcement.what: The block Vibisual injects into sessions that attached themselves through Claude Code hooks.
hookEnforcement.more: Vibisual did not start those sessions, so their instructions ride in on the hook channel each turn.
hookEnforcement.off: Hook-attached sessions stop receiving Vibisual's instructions.

plugins.what: The master switch for every enforcement plugin enabled in this project.
plugins.more: Each enabled plugin also gets its own row below, so you can keep some and drop others.
plugins.off: No plugin instructions are added at all, no matter which plugins are enabled.

plugin.more: You enabled this plugin in the Plugins window; it writes its rules into every prompt of this project.
plugin.off: Only this plugin stops being enforced — the others stay as they are.

claudeMd.what: Project instruction files Claude Code loads by itself — CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, AGENTS.md.
claudeMd.more: Found next to your project, in the folders above it, and in your home .claude folder. Click a file to read it here.
claudeMd.off: The session starts without your project's house rules (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS).

autoMemory.what: Claude Code's own memory index (MEMORY.md) for this folder.
autoMemory.more: Only the index is loaded every turn; the individual memory files are read when they are needed.
autoMemory.off: Claude Code starts without its notes from previous sessions (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY).

skills.what: The one-line blurbs of every skill and slash command available here.
skills.more: Only the name and description from each file's front matter is loaded — full bodies are read when a skill is actually used.
skills.off: Every skill and slash command is disabled for the session (--disable-slash-commands).

bundledSkills.what: Skills that ship inside Claude Code itself.
bundledSkills.more: They live in the executable, so their size cannot be measured from here.
bundledSkills.off: Claude Code runs without its built-in skills (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS).

workflows.more: Part of Claude Code, not of this project, so there is no file to show.
workflows.off: Those workflows are not offered to the agent (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS).

gitInstructions.what: Git guidance and the repository status summary Claude Code adds on its own.
gitInstructions.more: This is why the agent already knows your branch and which files are modified.
gitInstructions.off: The agent starts without git guidance or a status summary (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS).

subagentDefs.what: The subagent types this project defines in .claude/agents.
subagentDefs.more: Their descriptions ride inside the Agent tool's own description, which is why there is no switch for them.
subagentDefs.off: This one cannot be turned off here — it is only measured.

systemPrompt.what: Claude Code's own system prompt — the instructions that make it Claude Code.
systemPrompt.more: It lives inside the executable, so the number here is an estimate rather than a measurement.
systemPrompt.off: This one cannot be turned off. It is listed so the total is honest.

toolSchemas.what: The definitions of the tools this agent may call — Read, Edit, Bash and the rest.
toolSchemas.more: The tool list is owned by Agent Settings; shortening it there makes this number smaller.
toolSchemas.off: Change the tool list in Agent Settings instead — the switch here is locked.

mcp.what: Extra tools attached through MCP servers.
mcp.more: Each attached server adds its own tool definitions to every prompt.
mcp.off: Detach the server in Agent Settings instead — the switch here is locked.

hooks.what: The Claude Code hooks that let Vibisual see this session at all.
hooks.more: Registered in settings.json. They add almost no tokens, but every event travels through them.
hooks.off: Hooks are removed in settings.json, not here. Without them Vibisual stops seeing this session.

compactSelf.what: The window through which the agent itself asks to compact the conversation.
compactSelf.more: Shipped only to agents with “Let the agent compact during work” turned on. The compaction runs at the end of that turn, never mid-task.
compactSelf.off: The agent can no longer ask; only the window threshold and turn-boundary compaction remain. Nothing is injected, so this line costs zero tokens when off.

autoGoalSkills.what: The procedures written down from work this project keeps repeating.
autoGoalSkills.more: Only the name, one line of description and the file path are sent. The body stays in .vibisual/skills and the agent opens it when the work matches.
autoGoalSkills.off: The agent works each of those procedures out from scratch again.

codexInstructions.what: Project instructions Codex discovers in AGENTS.md and its override or fallback files.
codexInstructions.more: Read from the project instruction chain for this agent’s working directory. Global Codex instructions have their own row.
codexInstructions.off: Stops automatic loading of project instruction files on the next run. Global instructions and text already in this conversation remain.

codexGlobalInstructions.what: Personal instructions Codex loads from its home directory for every project.
codexGlobalInstructions.more: Comes from AGENTS.md or AGENTS.override.md in CODEX_HOME, usually ~/.codex. These are separate from project instructions.
codexGlobalInstructions.off: This row cannot be switched off here. Edit the global instruction file to change future runs; existing conversation text remains.

codexCollaborationInstructions.what: Codex’s built-in guidance for its collaboration mode.
codexCollaborationInstructions.more: Added by the Codex runtime according to the active collaboration mode.
codexCollaborationInstructions.off: Stops adding collaboration-mode instructions on the next run. Instructions already in this conversation remain.

codexSkills.what: The skill names and descriptions Codex makes available to the agent.
codexSkills.more: Discovered from Codex skill folders and enabled skill packages. A skill’s full instructions are read when it is used.
codexSkills.off: Disables skill discovery on the next run. Skill text already read in this conversation remains.

codexDeveloperInstructions.what: Additional instructions configured for Codex at the developer level.
codexDeveloperInstructions.more: Comes from the effective Codex developer_instructions setting for this working directory. Vibisual’s own prompt blocks have separate rows.
codexDeveloperInstructions.off: Omits configured developer instructions on the next run. Earlier instructions already in the conversation remain.

codexMcp.what: MCP servers explicitly registered in the effective Codex configuration.
codexMcp.more: Each configured server can supply tool definitions. This switch covers these configuration entries only; other detected servers have a separate row.
codexMcp.off: Disables configured servers on the next run without editing their configuration files. Turning this back on restores their configured state and does not enable individually disabled servers.

codexPlugins.what: Plugins explicitly registered in the effective Codex configuration.
codexPlugins.more: Comes from the plugin entries in the effective Codex settings. Other detected plugins have a separate row.
codexPlugins.off: Disables configured plugins on the next run without uninstalling them or editing configuration files. Turning this back on restores their configured state and keeps individually disabled plugins disabled.

codexHooks.what: Hooks registered with Codex, including integration hooks used by Vibisual.
codexHooks.more: Comes from Codex’s hook configuration. Hooks can add context when their events run.
codexHooks.off: Manage hook configuration separately. This row does not switch hooks off.

codexSystemPrompt.what: The core instructions and built-in tool definitions supplied by the Codex runtime.
codexSystemPrompt.more: Managed inside Codex. Its complete text and exact token cost are not exposed by this inventory.
codexSystemPrompt.off: This source cannot be switched off here.

codexRuntimeMcp.what: MCP servers detected outside the explicit configuration entries controlled above.
codexRuntimeMcp.more: Reported by Codex’s runtime inventory. These entries are not covered by the configured-server switch.
codexRuntimeMcp.off: This row cannot switch these servers off. Manage them through the Codex integration or settings that added them.

codexRuntimePlugins.what: Codex plugins detected outside the explicit configuration entries controlled above.
codexRuntimePlugins.more: Reported by Codex’s plugin inventory. These entries are not covered by the configured-plugin switch.
codexRuntimePlugins.off: This row cannot switch these plugins off. Manage them through the Codex integration or settings that added them.

vibisual.what: A block Vibisual writes into the prompt itself.
vibisual.more: Assembled fresh on every turn from what is on your canvas and in your settings.
vibisual.off: It is simply left out of the next prompt.

plugins.what: Rules an enforcement plugin adds to every prompt in this project.
plugins.more: Comes from the Plugins window — only the plugins you enabled are here.
plugins.off: That plugin's rules stop being sent.

memory.what: Something the agent remembers from earlier sessions.
memory.more: Read from the memory files of this project or this folder.
memory.off: The agent works from this conversation alone.

instructions.what: Instruction files the engine loads automatically.
instructions.more: Read from disk every time a session starts. Click a file to read it here.
instructions.off: The session starts without those instructions.

skills.what: Descriptions of the skills and commands the agent could call.
skills.more: Only the short blurbs are loaded; the full text is read when one is actually used.
skills.off: The agent no longer knows those are available.

tools.what: Definitions of the tools the agent may call.
tools.more: The list is owned by Agent Settings.
tools.off: Change it in Agent Settings — it cannot be turned off here.

system.what: Context the engine adds itself, outside this project.
system.more: Managed inside the engine; its full text or exact size may not be available.
system.off: This is not ours to turn off; it is measured so the total is honest.

orchestra.title: Orchestra
orchestra.about: When this is on, the agent you give an order to becomes the conductor for that turn: it decides what kind of request it is, whether to split the work, which agents to create and how to link them with edges, and which token-saving strategies fit. It reports that plan with its reasons before any member starts.
orchestra.effectiveOn: On for this agent — your next order will be conducted.
orchestra.effectiveOff: Off for this agent — orders go straight to it as usual.
orchestra.costWarning: Using several agents can cost more than one, not less — each member reads its own rules and files again. The conductor is told to answer directly when a request is small.

conductor.title: Conductor
conductor.about: The conductor is this agent itself, for that one turn — its saved settings are not changed. Its engine follows the agent (switching engines mid-session would break the session), so only the model and effort for each engine are set here.

field.memberIsolationHint: Every member is born in its own git worktree, so workers running side by side cannot collide on the same files. Merging the branches afterwards is yours to do. Claude members only — Codex has no matching flag.

permission.bypassHint: The conductor calls the local Vibisual API by itself, so it runs without prompts. It still cannot edit code — Write and Edit are removed for its turn.

member.title: Members
member.about: Members are the agents the conductor creates on the canvas. It reuses members from earlier runs first. Empty fields leave the choice to the conductor.

taskEdgePopup.templateTooltip: Select a preset pair. Picking one auto-fills Type, Gate, and all advanced options below.

taskEdgePopup.messageTooltip: The instruction sent to the target agent. Press Ctrl/Cmd+Enter to submit.
taskEdgePopup.typeTooltip: What this edge means — Command (instruction), Artifact (deliverable), Request (help ask), Critique (review). Edge color reflects this in the map.
taskEdgePopup.gateTooltip: Auto: runs as soon as saved. Manual: requires a human to press Run. Use Manual for anything destructive or high-impact.
taskEdgePopup.autoTooltip: Auto: executes immediately when the edge is saved. Fastest, but skips human review.
taskEdgePopup.manualTooltip: Manual: waits for a human to press Run. Safer for destructive or high-impact tasks.
taskEdgePopup.advancedTooltip: Message format / Return format / Timeout / Retry / Cache / Priority. Templates prefill these with sensible defaults — usually no change needed. (Execution logic is a future step; this version only stores the values.)
taskEdgePopup.advancedShow: Show advanced options: message format, return format, timeout, retry, cache, priority.
taskEdgePopup.messageFormatTooltip: Free: easy but ambiguous. Schema: key/value, structured. Prefer Schema for critical or repeatable tasks.
taskEdgePopup.freeTextTooltip: Free text: natural-language instruction. Fast to write, but the AI may misread nuance.
taskEdgePopup.schemaTooltip: Schema: structured key/value input. More upfront work, fewer downstream surprises.
taskEdgePopup.schemaEditTooltip: Open the schema editor. Type the format the source agent should follow when sending through this edge.
taskEdgePopup.schemaEditHint: Free-form text. The source agent will be told to format its outbound message in this shape. Leave empty to send as plain text.
taskEdgePopup.schemaPlaceholder:
Example:
{
  "goal": "...",
  "context": "...",
  "acceptance": ["..."]
}

— or natural-language —
Reply with: 1) what you changed, 2) which files, 3) any open risks.
taskEdgePopup.returnFormatTooltip: Artifact: actual file/diff paths. Summary: text summary only. Both: both. AI summaries can be wrong; prefer Artifact for anything you need to verify.
taskEdgePopup.artifactTooltip: Artifact: return the actual file path or diff. Verifiable by you.
taskEdgePopup.summaryTooltip: Summary: short text summary only. Fast, but AI summaries can be inaccurate.
taskEdgePopup.bothTooltip: Both: return the artifact and a summary so you can scan before diving in.
taskEdgePopup.timeoutTooltip: Max run duration in milliseconds. Leave blank for unlimited. Example: 60000 = 1 minute. Guards against runaway loops.
taskEdgePopup.retryTooltip: How many times to retry on failure. 0 = no retries. Useful for transient failures like network hiccups.
taskEdgePopup.retryDisabledNote: Coming soon — retry logic is not implemented yet. Value is saved as metadata only.
taskEdgePopup.priorityTooltip: Run order when multiple edges are ready. High runs first. Default Normal.
taskEdgePopup.priorityDisabledNote: Coming soon — priority scheduling is not implemented yet. Value is saved as metadata only.
taskEdgePopup.priorityLowTooltip: Low: runs only when nothing else is queued.
taskEdgePopup.priorityHighTooltip: High: jumps ahead of other pending edges.
taskEdgePopup.cacheTooltip: Reuse the previous result when inputs match (saves tokens). Turn OFF if the underlying data changes often.
taskEdgePopup.cacheLabelTooltip: When the input matches a previous run, reuse that result instead of re-running. Saves tokens. Turn OFF if underlying data changes often.
taskEdgePopup.cacheDisabledNote: Coming soon — result cache is not implemented yet. Value is saved as metadata only.
taskEdgePopup.delegationTooltip: STRICT: tasks matching this edge's purpose must be delegated through it. The source agent cannot handle them with its own Read/Grep. AUTO: the source agent decides whether to delegate based on cost and fit (3+ exploration steps / purpose match / target suitability). Simple 1-2 Read calls stay in-agent.
taskEdgePopup.delegationStrictTooltip: Mandatory delegation when the edge purpose matches. No self-handling. (Default)
taskEdgePopup.delegationAutoTooltip: The source agent decides autonomously based on exploration cost and fit.
taskEdgePopup.commandOptionsTooltip: Command-edge specifics (kind='command' only). Orthogonal to Delegation Policy: this controls the FORM of delegation, not whether it's enforced.
taskEdgePopup.commandModeTooltip: How tools are shared between parent and child. Shared: parent keeps every tool, can call directly or delegate. Tool delegation: tools the child has are stripped from the parent — delegation enforced naturally. Mode delegation: tools stay shared but the parent is instructed to delegate operations whose mode (plan / acceptEdits / specific model / skill) is the child's specialty.
taskEdgePopup.commandModeSharedTooltip: Parent keeps the tools. Both parent and child can run them. Delegation is recommended via prompt only. (Default — safest.)
taskEdgePopup.commandModeToolTooltip: Tools the child agent has are removed from the parent. The parent must dispatch via this edge to use them. (= Pre-v1.44 strict behavior.)
taskEdgePopup.commandModeModeTooltip: Parent keeps the tools, but the system prompt forces delegation of operations whose mode (plan / acceptEdits / specific model / skill) is the child's specialty. Pseudo-tool injection is a future round.
taskEdgePopup.commandModeModeNote: Mode delegation does not strip any tools — the parent is told via system prompt to delegate operations matching the child's mode. PreToolUse hook gating is planned for a follow-up.
taskEdgePopup.commandStripPreviewTooltip: Live computed: child agent's tools ∩ parent agent's tools. These are the tools the parent will lose access to when this edge is active.
taskEdgePopup.commandStripPreviewEmpty: No overlap — parent and child share no tools. Strip would be a no-op. Consider Mode delegation instead.
taskEdgePopup.cancelTooltip: Discard changes and close. The live preview on the canvas will revert.
taskEdgePopup.saveTooltip: Save these changes to the edge (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter).
taskEdgePopup.connectTooltip: Create the edge with these settings (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter).
taskEdgePopup.critiqueOptionsTip: Critique-edge only. Sets when to intervene (Timing) and what to enforce on reject (Authority). Ignored for other kinds.
taskEdgePopup.critiqueTimingTip: Intermediate (default): review at each milestone during the target's work. More frequent / safer / slower. Final: a single final review after completion. Less frequent / faster.
taskEdgePopup.critiqueTimingIntermediateTip: Intermediate: review at each milestone during the target's work. (default)
taskEdgePopup.critiqueTimingFinalTip: Final only: a single final review after the target completes.
taskEdgePopup.critiqueAuthorityTip: Force rework (default): on reject the target must redo the work. Exceeding Max Rework auto-downgrades to comment-only and escalates to the parent session. Comment only: reject is advisory only, no forced rework.
taskEdgePopup.critiqueAuthorityForceTip: Force rework: the target must redo on reject. (default)
taskEdgePopup.critiqueAuthorityCommentTip: Comment only: the target only takes the reject as a reference. No forced rework.
taskEdgePopup.critiqueMaxReworkTip: Max times the target may redo while in Force rework mode. Exceeding it auto-downgrades to comment-only and escalates to the parent session. A guard against infinite loops.
taskEdgePopup.critiqueMaxReworkActive: Max {{max}} times. Auto-downgrades to comment-only when exceeded.
